causal:influence:end_diastolic_volume:po.mechanism: Left-ventricular end-diastolic volume (EDV, preload) determines the degree of myocardial fibre stretch and LV cavity size at end-diastole; LV end-diastolic diameter is the echocardiographic linear dimension that directly indexes EDV. Dilated cardiomyopathy and volume overload increase both EDV and LV end-diastolic diameter simultaneously.

causal:influence:epinephrine:positive:al.mechanism: Elevated catecholamines (epinephrine, norepinephrine) stimulate respiratory rate and depth, producing hyperventilation and respiratory alkalosis

causal:influence:epinephrine:positive:ur.evidence: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology — pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma: diagnosis by elevated urinary fractionated catecholamines including epinephrine; Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (adrenal medullary catecholamine secretion and urinary excretion assay); Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (24-h urinary catecholamines as pheochromocytoma screening test) | intervention: pheochromocytoma (catecholamine-secreting tumour): do(epinephrine=high) -> urinary_epinephrine rises; DBH deficiency (OMIM 223360) as reciprocal evidence: do(epinephrine=absent) -> urinary_epinephrine absent
causal:influence:epinephrine:positive:ur.mechanism: plasma epinephrine is filtered and excreted by the kidney; a higher plasma epinephrine concentration drives proportionally greater urinary epinephrine excretion; pheochromocytoma-driven elevation of plasma epinephrine is reflected diagnostically in elevated urinary epinephrine

causal:influence:erythrocyte_23_bpg:nega.evidence: An increase in 2,3-DPG, which is an end product of red cell metabolism, shifts the curve to the right ... the unloading of O2 to peripheral tissues is assisted  ||  "There is a rightward shift of the O2 dissociation curve at moderate altitudes that results in a better unloading of O2 in venous blood at a given PO2. causal:influence:erythrocyte_pyrimidine_.evidence: Hemolytic anemia due to pyrimidine 5' nucleotidase deficiency (OMIM 266120, NT5C3A gene); PMC3878480 (About P5N deficiency — jaundice/neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia listed as clinical feature); Blood ASH 2005 PMC: functional analysis of NT5C3 mutants — haemolytic anaemia; Orphanet 35120 (clinical features include jaundice). Mechanism: pyrimidine nucleotide accumulation -> basophilic stippling, haemolysis -> bilirubin release -> unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia. | intervention: NT5C3A LoF: erythrocyte pyrimidine nucleotide pool rises -> haemolytic anaemia -> plasma unconjugated bilirubin increases
causal:influence:erythrocyte_pyrimidine_.mechanism: NT5C3A (pyrimidine 5'-nucleotidase 1) deficiency causes accumulation of pyrimidine nucleotides (UMP, CMP) in erythrocytes. Elevated erythrocyte pyrimidine nucleotides impair red cell energy metabolism, leading to chronic haemolytic anaemia. RBC haemolysis releases haemoglobin that is catabolised to unconjugated bilirubin (indirect bilirubin), causing jaundice/hyperbilirubinaemia. Elevated erythrocyte pyrimidine nucleotide pool -> haemolysis -> ↑plasma unconjugated bilirubin.

causal:influence:erythropoietin:positive.mechanism: EPO promotes survival/proliferation/differentiation of erythroid progenitors (BFU-E/CFU-E), raising RBC production

causal:influence:ferrochelatase_activity.evidence: Harrison's PIM, The Porphyrias (EPP: elevated erythrocyte free protoporphyrin); OMIM 177000 (EPP1: erythrocyte free PPIX elevated). causal:influence:ferrochelatase_activity.mechanism: Ferrochelatase deficiency (EPP) is the canonical cause of elevated erythrocyte free (non-zinc-chelated) protoporphyrin. Free protoporphyrin IX accumulates because the terminal heme-synthesis step is blocked. do(ferrochelatase_activity down) → erythrocyte free porphyrin rises.

causal:influence:ferrochelatase_activity.evidence: Harrison's PIM, The Porphyrias (EPP: FECH deficiency, elevated erythrocyte free protoporphyrin); OMIM 177000 (EPP1, FECH LoF); Orphanet J Rare Dis 2009 (EPP: erythrocyte PPIX markedly elevated). | intervention: Ferrochelatase (FECH) loss-of-function (erythropoietic protoporphyria, OMIM 177000)
causal:influence:ferrochelatase_activity.mechanism: Ferrochelatase (FECH) inserts Fe2+ into protoporphyrin IX to form heme (last step of heme biosynthesis). Deficiency (erythropoietic protoporphyria, EPP) causes protoporphyrin IX to accumulate in erythrocytes, rising to pathologically elevated concentrations.

causal:influence:follicular_pka_activity.mechanism: cAMP/PKA upregulates thyroglobulin, TPO and NIS expression and iodide organification (quality: PKA activity -> disposition: CREB-driven thyroid-gene transcription -> process: TPO/NIS expression + iodide organification -> quality: organification capacity)

Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 13

causal:influence:gcdh_activity:negative:.mechanism: GCDH deficiency causes glutaric acid accumulation; glutaric acid is hydroxylated to 3-hydroxyglutaric acid (3-OH-GA), which is the most sensitive biomarker of GCDH impairment — reduced GCDH raises urinary 3-hydroxyglutaric acid

causal:influence:gi_sympathetic_tone:neg.evidence: In general, stimulation of the sympathetic nervous system inhibits activity of the gastrointestinal tract... It exerts its effects in two ways: (1) to a slight extent by direct effect of secreted norepinephrine to inhibit intestinal tract smooth muscle... and (2) to a major extent by an inhibitory effect of norepinephrine on the neurons of the entire enteric nervous system.  ||  "Brunner's glands are inhibited by sympathetic stimulation; therefore, such stimulation in very excitable persons is likely to leave the duodenal bulb unprotected and is perhaps one of the factors that cause this area of the gastrointestinal tract to be the site of peptic ulcers" — Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, ch w21, p. 806
causal:influence:gi_sympathetic_tone:neg.mechanism: sympathetic inhibition of enteric neurons decreases GI secretion

causal:influence:glp1:negative:plasma_gl.mechanism: GLP-1 → paracrine alpha-cell GLP-1R signaling disposition → reduced glucagon secretion

causal:influence:glutathione_synthetase_.evidence: Glutathione synthetase deficiency OMIM 266130; PMC1852094 (Inborn errors in glutathione metabolism): 'elevated gamma-glutamylcysteine... blockade of glutathione synthesis causes functional loss of feedback inhibition on gamma-GCS, increasing flux'; PMID 4152248 (GSS deficiency original paper); Lehninger (gamma-glutamyl cycle, GSS step). | intervention: do(GSS loss-of-function) — glutathione synthetase deficiency OMIM 266130 [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:glutathione_synthetase_.mechanism: Glutathione synthetase (GSS) converts gamma-glutamylcysteine + glycine -> glutathione. GSS deficiency blocks glutathione synthesis; gamma-glutamylcysteine (the GSS substrate) accumulates and is excreted in urine. Additionally, loss of glutathione feedback inhibition on gamma-GCS causes overproduction of gamma-glutamylcysteine. do(GSS LoF) -> urinary gamma-glutamylcysteine rises.

causal:influence:haao_activity:positive:.evidence: Shi H et al. NEJM 2017 (doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1616361) — biallelic HAAO loss-of-function causes congenital NAD deficiency disorder with congenital malformations rescued by niacin supplementation; patient plasma showed increased 3-HAA and decreased NAD/NADH. GeneReviews NBK593504 (CNDD): HAAO, KYNU, and NADSYN1 are the three CNDD-causing genes, all essential for de novo NAD synthesis from tryptophan. Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (kynurenine pathway → quinolinate → NaMN via QPRT → NAD+; HAAO catalyses the penultimate step). | intervention: do(HAAO biallelic LoF) = congenital NAD deficiency disorder; HAAO activity falls → NAD+ and NADH levels fall | intervention: do(HAAO biallelic LoF) — congenital NAD deficiency disorder (CNDD), OMIM via Shi NEJM 2017
causal:influence:haao_activity:positive:.mechanism: 3-Hydroxyanthranilate 3,4-dioxygenase (HAAO) catalyses the committed step from 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid to alpha-amino-beta-carboxymuconate semialdehyde, which spontaneously cyclizes to quinolinate — the universal de novo precursor of the NAD+ pyridine ring. Biallelic HAAO LoF blocks de novo NAD+ biosynthesis from tryptophan (congenital NAD deficiency disorder, CNDD), reducing the total cellular NAD+ pool and consequently cellular NADH. Sign: more HAAO activity → more quinolinate flux → more NAD+ → more NADH (do(HAAO LoF) = NAD/NADH falls).

causal:influence:hdl_cholesterol:positiv.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (HDL reverse transport to liver via SR-BI); BioModels BIOMD0000000434 (McAuley2012)
causal:influence:hdl_cholesterol:positiv.mechanism: HDL reverse cholesterol transport -> SR-BI selective hepatic uptake of HDL cholesteryl esters -> delivery to hepatocyte pool

causal:influence:helper_t_cell_activatio.evidence: OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-42.2 (42.2: Adaptive Immune Response): helper T cells release cytokines that 'activate B cells'; Th2 cytokines (IL-4, IL-5, IL-13) drive humoral responses; antigen-presenting cells plus IL-4 polarise naïve CD4+ T cells to Th2 fate. | intervention: Antigenic stimulation / allergen exposure (do(helper_t_cell_activation)) increases Th2 activation and type-2 cytokine output; verified by allergy immunotherapy studies showing antigen drives Th2 responses
causal:influence:helper_t_cell_activatio.mechanism: Activated CD4+ helper T cells differentiate into Th2 effector cells under IL-4 cytokine milieu; increased helper T cell activation (antigen stimulation) drives Th2 polarization, raising Th2 cell activation rate and IL-4/IL-5/IL-13 secretion.

causal:influence:hepatocellular_injury:n.evidence: Serum cholinesterase is a hepatocyte-synthesis-dependent biomarker that falls with impaired hepatic synthetic capacity (cirrhosis: median 1590 vs 7886 IU/L in controls). Ramachandran J et al., 'Serum cholinesterase is an excellent biomarker of liver cirrhosis', Trop Gastroenterol 2014;35(1):15-20 (PMID:25276901, VERIFIED real); Boron & Boulpaep, Medical Physiology (hepatic synthetic function).
causal:influence:hepatocellular_injury:n.mechanism: Serum butyrylcholinesterase (BCHE / pseudocholinesterase) is synthesized almost exclusively by hepatocytes and continuously secreted into plasma; hepatocellular injury/necrosis (and the cirrhosis it drives) reduces functional hepatic synthetic mass, lowering BCHE production, so serum cholinesterase activity falls. A recognised marker of hepatic synthetic reserve (parallels falling albumin). do(increase hepatocellular injury) -> Delta serum cholinesterase down.

causal:influence:hepcidin:negative:ferro.evidence: Nemeth et al. 2004 Science 306:2090 (PMID 15514116); Parmar2019 BioModels MODEL1805140003 (PMID 30608934); Ganz & Nemeth 2012 BBA review | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-098 (17.11: Organs with Secondary Endocrine Functions): 'Hepcidins block the release of iron from cells in the body, helping to regulate iron homeostasis'; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-137 (23.8: Chemical Digestion and Absorption - A Closer Look): 'When the body needs iron...there is increased uptake of iron from the intestine and accelerated release of iron into the bloodstream' — low body iron reduces hepcidin, releasing ferroportin-mediated export (implied mechanism) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:hepcidin:negative:ferro.mechanism: hepcidin binds ferroportin on enterocytes/macrophages/hepatocytes, triggering its internalization and degradation, lowering cellular iron export

causal:influence:hexokinase_activity:pos.evidence: Williams Hematology (HK deficiency: non-spherocytic hemolytic anemia — glycolytic enzyme defect, OMIM 235700); Scriver's OMMBID (erythrocyte enzymopathies: HK1 deficiency causes chronic hemolytic anemia); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 14 (hexokinase: committed step of glycolysis). | intervention: HK1 loss-of-function (congenital hemolytic anemia, OMIM 235700): do(hexokinase_activity↓) → erythrocyte ATP depletion → hemolysis → red_cell_mass↓
causal:influence:hexokinase_activity:pos.mechanism: Erythrocyte hexokinase-1 (HK1) phosphorylates glucose to glucose-6-phosphate, the committed entry step into glycolysis in red cells. HK1 LoF (congenital non-spherocytic hemolytic anemia type I, OMIM 235700) → glycolytic failure in mature erythrocytes → ATP depletion → premature hemolysis → reduced red cell mass. HK activity ↑ → sustained glycolysis → RBC viability → red_cell_mass ↑.

causal:influence:hmg_coa_reductase_activ.evidence: HMGCR is the rate-limiting enzyme of cholesterol biosynthesis; rare LoF variants cause reduced cholesterol synthesis (statin pharmacology mimics LoF); reduced hepatic cholesterol synthesis on activity reduction
causal:influence:hmg_coa_reductase_activ.mechanism: RHEA:15989 (EC 1.1.1.34): (3S)-3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA (CHEBI:43074) + 2 NADPH + 2 H(+) = (R)-mevalonate (CHEBI:36464) + 2 NADP(+) + CoA [physiological direction; Rhea equation is written in reverse]; mevalonate is the committed product of the rate-limiting cholesterol synthesis step; hepatic cholesterol synthesis is the downstream process

causal:influence:hydroxyphenylpyruvate_d.evidence: OMIM 276710 (tyrosinemia type III, HPD deficiency): 4-hydroxyphenyllactic aciduria is a characteristic finding; Saudubray, Inborn Metabolic Diseases; Mughal et al., method validation for serum 4-hydroxyphenyllactate in tyrosinemia (PMC9259389) | intervention: Tyrosinemia type III (HPD loss-of-function, OMIM 276710)
causal:influence:hydroxyphenylpyruvate_d.mechanism: HPD deficiency (tyrosinemia type III) causes 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate accumulation; this ketoacid is reduced by lactate dehydrogenase to 4-hydroxyphenyllactate (p-hydroxyphenyllactic acid), which accumulates in plasma — reduced HPD activity raises plasma 4-hydroxyphenyllactate

causal:influence:hydroxyphenylpyruvate_d.evidence: OMIM 276710 (tyrosinemia type III, HPD deficiency): 4-hydroxyphenyllactic aciduria is a diagnostic feature; Saudubray, Inborn Metabolic Diseases; Mughal et al. (PMC9259389) | intervention: Tyrosinemia type III (HPD loss-of-function, OMIM 276710)
causal:influence:hydroxyphenylpyruvate_d.mechanism: HPD deficiency (tyrosinemia type III) causes 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate accumulation and secondary 4-hydroxyphenyllactate production via LDH reduction; 4-hydroxyphenyllactate is excreted in urine — reduced HPD activity raises urinary hydroxyphenyllactate

MCH antagonists inhibit feeding in several species" — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 40, p 1569
causal:influence:hypothalamic_mch_level:.mechanism: MCH neurons in lateral hypothalamus signal to increase feeding; MCH peptide administration acutely increases food intake

causal:influence:il1beta:positive:il6.mechanism: IL-1beta engages IL-1R -> MyD88/NF-kB -> IL-6 production (TNF and IL-1 synergistically induce IL-6)

[citations PubMed-verified]

causal:influence:il6:positive:crh.mechanism: circulating IL-6 stimulates hypothalamic CRH secretion, a major driver of the inflammation-evoked HPA response

causal:influence:intracellular_atp:negat.evidence: OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-7.7 (7.7: Regulation of Cellular Respiration): 'When adequate ATP and NADH levels are available, the rates of these reactions [isocitrate and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase] decrease' (Table 7.1).

Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 19, p 683
causal:influence:intratesticular_testost.mechanism: intratesticular testosterone binds AR on Sertoli cells and peritubular myoid cells, supporting spermatocyte meiosis completion, spermiogenesis, and spermiation

causal:influence:isobutyryl_coa_dehydrog.evidence: Isobutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency, OMIM:611283 — plasma C4 acylcarnitine (isobutyrylcarnitine) is the primary NBS flag for ACAD8 deficiency
causal:influence:isobutyryl_coa_dehydrog.mechanism: RHEA:44180 (EC 1.3.8.5): 2-methylpropanoyl-CoA is the substrate; accumulated isobutyryl-CoA is transesterified to carnitine by CPT enzymes, producing isobutyrylcarnitine (C4-acylcarnitine) measurable in plasma by tandem MS

causal:influence:isovaleryl_coa_dehydrog.evidence: Scriver's OMMBID / Saudubray — isovaleric acidemia (IVD, OMIM 243500): mitochondrial toxicity of accumulated isovaleryl-CoA; IVD is an ETF-dependent dehydrogenase (same ETF pathway as GCDH, MCAD, SCHAD). Lehninger Ch.18: acyl-CoA dehydrogenases donate electrons to ETF for ETC entry. Ensenauer et al. (2004) Pediatr Res: mitochondrial dysfunction in isovaleric acidemia. | intervention: Isovaleric acidemia (IVD LoF, OMIM 243500): ETF electron flux from leucine catabolism impaired; isovaleryl-CoA mitochondrial toxicity → cellular ATP level reduced
causal:influence:isovaleryl_coa_dehydrog.mechanism: IVD (isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenase) catalyses the FAD-linked dehydrogenation of isovaleryl-CoA in leucine catabolism; electrons are transferred via ETF to ETF-QO and then ubiquinone in the mitochondrial ETC, contributing to ATP synthesis. IVD deficiency (isovaleric acidemia) impairs this electron-flux pathway, and accumulated isovaleryl-CoA/isovalerate exerts mitochondrial toxicity. do(IVD_activity UP) → more ETF electron flux from leucine catabolism → ETC → more cellular ATP.

causal:influence:ivd_activity:negative:p.evidence: PMC2652706 (isovaleric acidemia, IVD deficiency, OMIM 243500; elevated plasma C5 isovalerylcarnitine is the primary biomarker); MDPI Metabolites 2020 PMC7548899 (NBS C5 elevation in IVA) | intervention: IVD LoF (isovaleric acidemia, OMIM 243500)
causal:influence:ivd_activity:negative:p.mechanism: IVD (isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenase) oxidizes isovaleryl-CoA in leucine catabolism; LoF causes isovaleryl-CoA accumulation and conjugation to carnitine as isovalerylcarnitine (C5), elevating plasma C5 acylcarnitine — the hallmark NBS marker of isovaleric acidemia

causal:influence:kisspeptin:positive:gnr.evidence: "administration of kisspeptin restored estrous cyclicity, ovulation, and circulating LH and FSH levels... kisspeptin administration to women with hyperprolactinemia-induced hypothalamic amenorrhea was shown to reactivate gonadotropin secretion." Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 8, p 193  ||  "KISS1R, which encodes the receptor for kisspeptin 1/metastin, an important GnRH stimulatory neuropeptide particularly at the time of puberty (2–5%)" [of CHH mutations] — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 19, p. 729
causal:influence:kisspeptin:positive:gnr.mechanism: Kisspeptin binds KISS1R on GnRH neurons → GnRH release; administration restores estrous cyclicity and gonadotropin secretion suppressed by hyperprolactinemia

causal:influence:kynureninase_activity:n.evidence: PMID 17334708; (Abstract; Xanthurenic aciduria due to a mutation in KYNU encoding kynureninase (2007)); “Massive urinary excretion of xanthurenic acid, 3-hydroxykynurenine and kynurenine...suggested kynureninase deficiency.” | KYNU loss-of-function (a clean genetic do()) causes massive urinary 3-hydroxykynurenine, so kynureninase activity decreases urinary 3-hydroxykynurenine (sign -). [citations PubMed-verified]

causal:influence:lcat_activity:positive:.evidence: Glomset JA. The plasma lecithin:cholesterol acyltransferase reaction. J Lipid Res. 1968;9(2):155-167; OMIM 245900 (familial LCAT deficiency); Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, Disorders of Lipoprotein Metabolism; PMC3373316 (LCAT deficiency, HDL-C very low). Intervention: LCAT loss-of-function (OMIM 245900): do(LCAT activity down) -> plasma HDL-cholesterol severely reduced. | intervention: LCAT loss-of-function (familial LCAT deficiency, OMIM 245900)
causal:influence:lcat_activity:positive:.mechanism: LCAT (lecithin-cholesterol acyltransferase) esterifies free cholesterol on nascent HDL particles, driving their maturation from small pre-beta HDL3 to large alpha-HDL2; the resulting cholesteryl-ester-enriched core stabilises the HDL particle. LCAT deficiency (familial LCAT deficiency, OMIM 245900; fish-eye disease, OMIM 136120) abolishes HDL maturation, producing a severe fall in plasma HDL-cholesterol with accumulation of abnormal lipid-poor nascent HDL discs.

causal:influence:left_atrial_pressure:ne.evidence: "left atrial pressure rises and the flaplike foramen ovale quickly closes. A rise in aortic pressure... also increases left atrial pressure." (West's Respiratory Physiology, 11th ed., ch 9)
